root_motivation: Give contested-claim reasoning a shared, machine-readable evidence base that is structurally forced to represent multiple stances before any LLM reasoning begins. Without a stable Corpus schema the steelman/cruxes/bridge LLM stages have nothing honest to operate on.
user_persona: Joe Yen, running wintermute automation on his Arch Linux laptop; invokes `concord corpus build '<claim>'` to seed a perspective-diverse source set before feeding it into LLM reasoning stages.

acceptance_criteria.description: `cargo build` and `cargo test` are green in a fresh ~/wintermute/concord workspace; `concord --help` lists the `corpus` subcommand. MSRV 1.85, no let-chains.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac1.rs — assert `concord --help` exits 0 and output contains 'corpus'

acceptance_criteria.description: `concord corpus build '<claim>' --fixtures tests/fixtures/<case>` produces a Corpus JSON validating against the documented schema, with every Source carrying a Stance and a provenance record.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac2.rs — build with fixture dir, deserialize output, assert schema validity

acceptance_criteria.description: The dedup pass collapses a fixture set containing 3 syndicated copies of one article into a single retained Source (asserted in a unit test on the fixture corpus).
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac3.rs — unit test on dedup with fixture containing 3 near-identical sources

acceptance_criteria.description: Stance tagging assigns the correct Stance to >=80% of a hand-labelled, independently authored fixture set (>=15 sources spanning >=2 stances). Labels live in checked-in expected.json written before the tagger.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac4.rs — load fixtures + expected.json, run tagger, assert accuracy >= 0.80

acceptance_criteria.description: No code path in the default `build` reaches the network unless a real gatherer is explicitly configured; test suite runs with networking unavailable and passes. A test asserts the FixtureGatherer path performs zero outbound connections.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac5.rs — run corpus build --fixtures without network, assert exit 0 and no net calls

acceptance_criteria.description: `main()` calls `sigpipe::reset()` first; `concord corpus show <file> | head` does not panic.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/acceptance_ac6.rs — pipe concord corpus show through head, assert exit without panic

scope: Cargo workspace at ~/wintermute/concord with concord-corpus lib crate and concord binary
SourceGatherer trait + FixtureGatherer implementation (no outbound network in tests)
Shingled-token Jaccard dedup above tunable threshold
Rule-based credibility scoring (has-author, has-date, primary-vs-secondary, domain-class)
CLI: `concord corpus build`, `concord corpus show`, `concord corpus stats`
non_goals: Crux vs misunderstanding classification (lands in concord-cruxes)
Outbound web search/fetch in the default test path (FixtureGatherer only)
ML-based credibility oracle (rule-based heuristic only, human-overridable)

additional.workspace: true — must be a real cargo workspace so sibling PRDs can add member crates
additional.no_let_chains: true — per self_recall_baseline_gate_red, MSRV 1.85 excludes let-chains
additional.sigpipe_reset: true — first line of main() per self_sigpipe_panic_toolkit

five_whys_trace.q: Why build concord-corpus rather than extending an existing research tool?
five_whys_trace.a: Existing research tools (like /deep-research) converge on one answer; concord-corpus inverts that — it deliberately spreads across stances to avoid single-framing collapse.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does stance-diversity require its own data structure rather than just tagging search results?
five_whys_trace.a: A Corpus is the shared contract for every downstream stage (steelman, cruxes, bridge). Without a stable, tested schema those LLM stages have nothing honest to reason over — they'd be reasoning over raw search results with no provenance.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the corpus be LLM-free in this first PRD?
five_whys_trace.a: LLM-free keeps the foundation deterministic and cloud-build-safe. If the schema and dedup are themselves LLM-dependent, validating them is circular — you'd be checking LLM output with LLM output.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the workspace need to be a real cargo workspace rather than a standalone crate?
five_whys_trace.a: Four sibling PRDs (steelman, cruxes, bridge, deescalate) are rust-extend PRDs with build_into: ~/wintermute/concord. They add member crates. A standalone crate cannot accept `cargo workspace member` additions cleanly.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should rust_edition be 2021 or 2024?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: 2021 — MSRV is 1.85; edition 2024 requires 1.85+ but the scaffold template defaults to 2024. PRD says 'Rust 2021' explicitly.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the binary live relative to the workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The concord binary is a [[bin]] in concord-corpus/Cargo.toml (not a separate crate). Sibling crates (steelman etc.) add their own members. The workspace root Cargo.toml lists members.
